STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from Abraham’s episode and prayer, which asks security for Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, and prosperity for his progeny.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.anchor: the security of Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, prosperity for his progeny

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.claim: Abraham also prayed for forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.anchor: forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's prayers concern Makkah and his children settled there, showing Quraysh that their lives oppose his hopes while Muhammad and his followers fulfill them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The purpose is to make evident to the Quraysh that the whole life that they are leading is totally against the supplications and desires of Abraham (sws).

ASAD-NOTES:14:38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:38/r1.claim: Abraham acknowledges that God knows what is hidden inwardly and what is public, and that nothing on earth or in heaven is concealed from Him.
ASAD-NOTES:14:38/r1.anchor: Thou truly knowest all that we may hide [in our hearts] as well as all that we bring into the open

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The statement's eloquence lies in covering what a supplicant cannot articulate or feels shy to express, since God's knowledge includes both hidden and apparent things.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This sentence has included all such things because the knowledge of God extends to all that is hidden and all that is apparent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi counts Rabbi or Rabbana seven times and says the apparent repetition is essential to supplication, which repeatedly humbles itself and seeks God's attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This apparently seems a repetition. Yet this is a feature of a supplication; in fact, it is essential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbi presents as grounds for the plea a favour of God the supplicant has personally experienced.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication the favour of God he has experienced.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbana presents as grounds for the plea a favour witnessed by all God's creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prayer is retold to Quraysh so they remember why they were settled in the barren valley, recognize Abraham's prayer as the source of their blessings, and see that they wrongly credit their alleged deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this supplication has been narrated to the Quraysh so that they recall the reason for being settled in this barren stretch of land

IBNHIBBAN:60/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:60/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNHIBBAN:60/r1.claim: Aisha calls it a grave lie to claim Muhammad saw his Lord, concealed revelation, or knew tomorrow; this frames the verse’s contrast between prophetic limits and Allah’s knowledge.
IBNHIBBAN:60/r1.anchor: عن مسروق بن الأجدع أنه سمع عائشة تقول: أعظم الفرية على الله من قال: إن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى ربه

IBNHIBBAN:870/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:870/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:870/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s saying that nothing is more honored before Allah than supplication, a virtue pertinent to Abraham’s prayer in this verse.
IBNHIBBAN:870/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ليس شيء أكرم على الله من الدعاء»

NASHR:v2p460/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p460/r1.speaker: الخطابي
NASHR:v2p460/r1.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī reads “evil is not from You” as etiquette in praise: attribute beautiful matters to God and avoid attributing low or ugly creatures to Him, though He created all and His power encompasses all.
NASHR:v2p460/r1.anchor: والشر ليس إليك: الإرشاد إلى استعمال الأدب في الثناء على الله

NASHR:v2p460/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p460/r2.speaker: الخطابي
NASHR:v2p460/r2.claim: The phrase is not intended to deny that God creates and governs evil; both good and evil issue from His creation and power.
NASHR:v2p460/r2.anchor: ولم يقع القصد به إلى إثبات شيء وإدخاله تحت قدرته ونفي ضده عنها فإن الخير والشر صادران عن خلقه

NASHR:v2p460/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p460/r3.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
NASHR:v2p460/r3.claim: Muslim ibn Yasār says that someone asking a king for a need would be glad to humble himself before him; Ibn Abī Shayba transmits the report.
NASHR:v2p460/r3.anchor: لو كنت بين يدي ملك تطلب حاجة لسرك أن تخشع له

NASHR:v2p460/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p460/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p460/r4.claim: A Bukhārī report from Ibn ʿAbbās advises avoiding forced rhyming in supplication; al-Ghazālī explains that affected rhyme conflicts with humility, though effortless balanced phrases in transmitted prayers are acceptable.
NASHR:v2p460/r4.anchor: وانظر إلى السجع من الدعاء فاجتنبه فإني عهدت رسول الله

NASHR:v2p460/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p460/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p460/r5.claim: Supplication should begin and end with praise of God, with blessings on the Prophet afterward; Abraham’s prayer models praise before asking, moving from God’s knowledge and gifts to the request that he and his descendants establish prayer.
NASHR:v2p460/r5.anchor: الثناء على الله تعالى أولا وآخرا أي قبل الدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r1.claim: Repeated calls express entreaty and reliance; Abu Hayyan sees no apparent difference between addressing God as “my Lord” and “our Lord.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r1.anchor: كرر النداء للتضرع والالتجاء، ولا يظهر تفاوت بين إضافة رب إلى ياء المتكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r2.claim: The hidden and manifest matters are general, covering whatever the speakers conceal or disclose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r2.anchor: وما نخفي وما نعلن عام فيما يخفونه وما يعلنونه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r3.claim: One explanation takes the hidden matter as grief at the separation and the open matter as their crying and prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: ما نخفي من الوجد لما وقع بيننا من الفرقة، وما نعلن من البكاء والدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r4.claim: Another account connects the hidden grief and public farewell to Hajar asking whom they were being left with; Abraham said God would care for them, and she asked whether God had commanded it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: ما نخفي من كآبة الافتراق، وما نعلن مما جرى بينه وبين هاجر حين قالت له عند الوداع: إلى من تكلنا؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the statement that nothing is hidden from God as Abraham’s speech: it expands from what the family hides to all things in earth and heaven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء، من كلام إبراهيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r6.claim: An alternative treats this statement as God’s confirmation of Abraham’s words, by analogy with the phrase “and thus they do.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: وما يخفى الآية من كلام الله عز وجل تصديقا لإبراهيم عليه السلام كقوله تعالى: وكذلك يفعلون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r7.claim: The reported prayers were not all uttered at one time: Isaac was not yet born when Hajar and Ishmael were left in Mecca, so the praise for both sons came later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p448#2/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الجمل التي تكلم بها إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لم تقع منه في زمان واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.claim: The words concern hidden and public needs and other matters. Al-Ālūsī’s preferred reading is the general one: God knows everything concealed or disclosed, including states unknown to Abraham himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r1.anchor: والظاهر العموم وهو المختار والمراد بما نخفي على ماقيل مايقابل ( مانعلن )

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī that Abraham hid his love for Ishmael and his mother and openly showed Sarah estrangement toward them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن إبراهيم النخعي أن مراده عليه السلام مانخفى من حب إسماعيل وأمه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.claim: One explanation is that Abraham hid his grief over the separation and openly wept and prayed.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : ما نخفي من الوجد لما وقع بيننا من الفرقة وما نعلن من البكاء والدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is the concealed sorrow of parting and the farewell exchange in which Hājar asked whom they were being left to and Abraham answered, ‘God.’
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : مانخفي من كآبة الافتراق ومانعلن مما جرى بيننا وبين هاجر عند الوداع

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.claim: In the reported explanations, mā is a relative pronoun with an omitted antecedent; another analysis makes it a verbal noun, ‘our secret as our public.’
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r5.anchor: و ( ما ) في جميع هذه الاقوال موصولة والعائد محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.claim: Putting the hidden before the manifest emphasizes equal divine knowledge: hiddenness receives priority, or secrecy precedes public disclosure and thus its knowing comes first.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r6.anchor: وتقديم ( مانخفى ) على ( مانعلن ) لتحقيق المساواة بينهما في تعلق العلم على أبلغ وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.claim: Mentioning known needs is not because God lacks knowledge; it displays servitude, humility, dependence, and eagerness for generosity. One reported rationale says God knows their interests and is more merciful than they are to themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r7.anchor: ليس لكونها غير معلومة لك بل إنما هو لأظهار العبودية والتخشع لعظمتك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.speaker: السهروردي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.claim: Al-Suhrawardī’s cited verse expresses that one need not complain to God, who already knows the complaint before it is spoken.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r8.anchor: وقد أشار السهر وردي إلى أن ظهور الحال يغني عن السؤال بقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r9.claim: Repeating the address intensifies humble pleading; the plural pronoun encompasses all hidden things in the kingdom and dominion, as the following clause clarifies.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p240#2/r9.anchor: وتكرير النداء للمبالغة في الضراعة والابتهال وضمير الجماعة كما قال بعض المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r1.claim: God’s knowledge is intrinsic, so one known thing does not differ from another in relation to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r1.anchor: لما أن علمه تعالى ذاتي فلا يتفاوت بالنسبة اليه معلوم دون معلوم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects to Abū Ḥayyān’s claim that no difference appears between ‘my Lord’ and ‘our Lord’ here; the preceding discussion explains why the plural address is apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : لايظهر تفاوت بين اضافة رب إلى ياء المتكلم وبين اضافته إلى جمع المتكلم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r3.claim: The clause says nothing is hidden from God rather than merely listing what is in the heavens and earth, stressing that divine knowledge has no trace of the obscurity found in creaturely knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r3.anchor: تحقيقا لما عناه بقوله : ( تعلم مانخفي ) من أن علمه تعالى بذلك ليس على وجه يكون فيه شائبة خفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r4.claim: Fī most naturally modifies an omitted adjective of shayʾ, ‘anything located in them,’ whether by residence or as part of them; attaching it to yakhfā is possible but strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r4.anchor: وكلمة ( في ) متعلقة بمحذوف وقع صفة لشيء أي لشيء كائن فيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r5.claim: Al-samāʾ includes all the heavens; earth precedes heaven because it is nearer to us, though they may also mean the lower and upper directions.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r5.anchor: باعتبار القرب والبعد منا المستعدين للتفاوت بالنسبة إلى علومنا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r6.claim: The shift from direct address to the name Allah signals the reason and universality of the rule: the knowledge applies to every thing, not just Abraham and his family.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r6.anchor: والالتفات من الخطاب إلى الاسم الجليل للاشعار بعلة الحكم والايذان بعمومه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r7.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r7.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī treats this as a divine parenthesis confirming Abraham, comparable to God’s parenthetical ‘and so they do’; most commentators instead take it as Abraham’s speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p241/r7.anchor: وعن الجبائي أن هذا من كلام الله تعالى شأنه وارد بطريق الاعتراض لتصديقه عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r1.claim: The matters Abraham conceals and makes public are their affairs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r1.anchor: {ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن} من أمورنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil explain these feelings as longing for Ishmael and his mother after Abraham settled them in the barren valley.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومقاتل: من الوجد بإسماعيل وأمه حيث أسكنتهما بواد غير ذي زرع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r3.claim: One view treats this as a continuation of Abraham's speech.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r4.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r4.claim: Most commentators take the statement about God's knowledge as God's own speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p357#2/r4.anchor: وقال الأكثرون: يقول الله عز وجل: {وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء}

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r1.claim: God knows their hidden and open states, interests, and needs, and is more merciful than they are to themselves; prayer expresses servitude, dependence on mercy, and eagerness for what He has.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r1.anchor: تعلم سرنا كما تعلم علننا، والمعنى إنك أعلم بأحوالنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r2.claim: Alternatively, they hide grief at separation and openly show supplication and reliance on God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r2.anchor: ما نخفي من وجد الفرقة وما نعلن من التضرع إليك والتوكل عليك

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r3.claim: Repeating the invocation intensifies pleading and turning to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r3.anchor: وتكرير النداء للمبالغة في التضرع واللجأ إلى الله تعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r4.claim: Nothing is hidden from God because His essential knowledge relates equally to every object of knowledge; min denotes totality.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:38/r4.anchor: لأنه العالم بعلم ذاتي يستوي نسبته إلى كل معلوم، ومن للاستغراق.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r1.claim: After praying for pure faith and provision that enables gratitude, Ibrāhīm notes that his descendants have opposed his aims; the renewed address presses for sincerity and a successful answer.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r1.anchor: ولما فرغ من الدعاء بالأهم من الإبقاء على الفطرة الأولى المشوقة للعزائم إلى العكوف في دارة الأنس , ومن الكفاية لهم المعاش , المنتج للشكر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r2.claim: God knows everything people conceal and disclose, since His power and knowledge encompass all things.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r2.anchor: أي جميع ما { نخفي وما نعلن } ثم أشار إلى عموم علمه فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r3.claim: The generic “anything” and repeated negation across earth and heaven emphatically universalize God's knowledge; He needs no information from prayer, which instead manifests servitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r3.anchor: من ذلك ولا غيره { في الأرض } ولما كان في سياق المبالغة , أعاد النافي تأكيدا

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says what Abraham hid was love for Ishmael and Hajar, while what was public was outward harshness toward them.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي} من حب إسماعيل وأمه {وما نعلن} قال: وما نظهر من الجفاء لهما

BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r1.claim: Abraham discloses needs not to inform God, who already knows them, but to display servitude and need for mercy and hasten divine gifts.
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r1.anchor: مقصده إن إظهار هذه الحاجات ليس لكونها غير معلومة لك

BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r2.claim: Nothing is hidden from God at any time; past, present, and future do not apply to Him, and His essential knowledge relates equally to all known things, unlike acquired human or angelic knowledge.
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r2.anchor: وما يخفي دائما إذ لا ماضي ولا مستقبل ولا حال بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r3.claim: Min is exhaustive; the phrase says no thing in earth or heaven escapes God, so He should do what benefits them.
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r3.anchor: من للاستغراق شيء ما في الأرض ولا في السماء لأنه العالم بعلم ذاتي

BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r4.claim: In the earth and heaven may modify is hidden or describe a thing located there.
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r4.anchor: فالظرف متعلق بيخفى أو شيء ما كائن فيهما على أنه صفة لشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r1.claim: This turn to God gathers up the preceding account: human misguidance and response, settling Abraham's sons by the House, and prayers for prayer and gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r1.anchor: جاء بهذا التوجه إلى الله جامعا لما في ضميره ، وفذلكة للجمل الماضية لما اشتملت عليه من ذكر ضلال كثير من الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r2.claim: The statement teaches Abraham's household and followers that God's knowledge is universal, so they should be watchful in every state and make their intentions sincere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r2.anchor: وفيه تعليم لأهله وأتباعه بعموم علم الله تعالى حتى يراقبوه في جميع الأحوال ويخلصوا النية إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r3.claim: The final clause is a tailpiece explaining that God knows everything; it uses the divine name to stand independently like a comprehensive maxim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p242/r3.anchor: ولكونها تذييلا أظهر فيها اسم الجلالة ليكون التذييل مستقلا بنفسه بمنزلة المثل والكلام الجامع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r1.claim: Abraham's concise prayer entrusts to God's knowledge his desires, including guidance and care for his children; he turns to praising God's complete knowledge and thanking Him for His gifts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r1.anchor: مقصد إبراهيم عليه السلام بقوله: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r2.claim: These verses teach that God's knowledge of things is fully detailed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r2.anchor: وهذه من الآيات المعلمة أن علم الله تعالى بالأشياء هو على التفصيل التام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p368/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p368/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p368/r1.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that Abraham concealed his anguish at leaving Ishmael and openly showed his love for him; the commentators place the words when Ishmael was settled in the sanctuary and Abraham was about to leave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p368/r1.anchor: قال أبو صالح عن ابن عباس ما نخفي من الوجد بمفارقة إسماعيل وما نعلن من الحب له قال المفسرون إنما قال هذا لما نزل إسماعيل الحرم وأراد فراقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r1.claim: Ibn Jarīr explains that Abraham says God knows his hidden and public intentions, including that his prayer for the people of this town seeks only God's pleasure and sincere devotion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r1.anchor: قال ابن جرير: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن إبراهيم خليله أنه قال: {ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن} أي: أنت تعلم قصدي في دعائي

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r23.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r23.claim: One view says the concealed and public matters include all their affairs.

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r24.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham hid grief for Ishmael and made his apprehension public.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r24.anchor: ما نخفي من الوجد بإسماعيل، وما نعلن من حذر، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v5p3885/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r25.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r25.claim: Al-Asamm identifies their hidden and public matter as monotheism; another report says Abraham hid grief at parting from Ishmael and openly said he had settled them there.
JISHUMI:v5p3885/r25.anchor: ما نخفي وما نعلن من التوحيد، عن الأصم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r1.claim: Repeating the address signals Abraham's pleading and appeal to God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r1.anchor: النداء المكرر دليل التضرع واللجأ إلى الله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r2.claim: God knows private and public matters without distinction, knows their needs better than they do, and is more merciful and more concerned for them; prayer expresses servitude, humility, dependence, hope for favor, and longing for mercy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r2.anchor: { إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن } تعلم السر كما تعلم العلن علما لا تفاوت فيه ، لأن غيبا من الغيوب لا يحتجب عنك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r3.claim: A person delayed in receiving a favor told a generous man that a request to someone like him was not a reminder of forgetfulness, but need compels a person to speak.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r3.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أنه رفع حاجته إلى كريم فأبطأ عليه النجح ، فأراد أن يذكره فقال : مثلك لا يذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r4.claim: One explanation is that Abraham hid grief at their separation and made his weeping and prayer public.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : ما تخفي من الوجد لما وقع بينا من الفرقة ، وما نعلن من البكاء والدعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r5.claim: Another report ties the hidden grief to Abraham's parting from Hagar: when she asked whom he was leaving them to, he answered God; she asked whether God commanded it, and accepted that they would be safe with Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : ما نخفي من كآبة الافتراق ، وما نعلن : يريد ما جرى بينه وبين هاجر حين قالت له عند الوداع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r6.claim: The statement may be God's words affirming Abraham, as in 27:34, or Abraham's own assertion that nothing anywhere is hidden from the Knower of the unseen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r6.anchor: كقوله : { وكذالك يفعلون } ( النمل : 34 ) أو من كلام إبراهيم ، يعني : وما يخفى على الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r7.claim: Min is exhaustive: the phrase means no thing at all is hidden from God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p525#2/r7.anchor: ( ومن ) للاستغراق ، كأنه قيل : وما يخفى عليه شيء ما

MUQATIL:14:38-39/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r1.claim: What Ibrahim hid was his distress about Ishmael being in a foreign land without livelihood or water.
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r1.anchor: من أمر إسماعيل في نفسي من الجزع عليه

MUQATIL:14:38-39/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r2.claim: What Ibrahim made known was his statement that he settled descendants in a barren valley, meaning Mecca.

MUQATIL:14:38-39/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r3.claim: Nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God.
MUQATIL:14:38-39/r3.anchor: وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.claim: Repeating the address Rabbana signals supplication and appeal to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r1.anchor: النداء المكرر دليل التضرع واللجأ إلى الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r2.claim: God knows what is secret just as He knows what is public.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.claim: The statement that nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden may be God's speech, confirming Abraham's words.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r3.anchor: من كلام الله عز وجل تصديقا لإبراهيم عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the statement may continue as Abraham's speech.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.claim: Min is comprehensive: nothing whatsoever is hidden from God.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#2/r5.anchor: ومن للاستغراق كأنه قيل وما يخفى على الله شيء ما

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r1.claim: Nothing about their circumstances is hidden from God.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r1.anchor: أي ليس يخفى عليك شيء من أحوالنا

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say Abraham’s concealed and public feeling was his longing for Ismail and Hajar after settling them in a barren valley.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r2.anchor: ابن عباس ومقاتل: تعلم جميع ما أخفيه وما أعلنه من الوجد بإسمعيل وأمه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r3.claim: One view treats the statement that nothing is hidden from God in earth or heaven as Abraham’s speech.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r4.claim: Another view makes it God’s response after Abraham says that He knows what they conceal and disclose.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول الله تعالى لما قال إبراهيم: { ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن }

QASHANI:14:35-38/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:35-38/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:35-38/r11.claim: What is hidden is what remains potential in us; what is declared is the perfections brought into actuality, and God knows both the earth of capacity and the heaven of spirit.
QASHANI:14:35-38/r11.anchor: مما فينا بالقوة { وما نعلن } مما أخرجناه إلى الفعل من الكمالات

RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r1.claim: After asking for his descendants' provisions, Abraham acknowledges that he does not know future outcomes; God knows their conditions, interests, and harms better than they do.
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r1.anchor: وأنه تعالى هو العالم بها المحيط بأسرارها ، فقال : { ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن } والمعنى : أنك أعلم

RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r2.claim: One interpretation says Abraham concealed his longing over separation from Ishmael and made his crying public.
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r2.anchor: قيل : ما نخفي من الوجد بسبب حصول الفرقة بيني وبين إسماعيل ، وما نعلن من البكاء

RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r3.claim: Another interpretation says he hid grief in his heart and refers publicly to his farewell exchange with Hajar: he said God would care for them; she asked whether God commanded it, and, hearing yes, said they need not fear.
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r3.anchor: وقيل : ما نخفي من الحزن المتمكن في القلب وما نعلن يريد ما جرى بينه وبين هاجر

RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r4.claim: One reading takes the next clause as God's confirmation of Abraham, as in Qur'an 16:34.
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r4.anchor: أنه كلام الله عز وجل تصديقا لإبراهيم عليه السلام كقوله : { وكذالك يفعلون } ( النحل : 34 )

RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r5.claim: Alternatively, Abraham continues speaking: nothing anywhere is hidden from the Knower of the unseen; the word min makes the statement exhaustive, not a single thing being hidden.
RAZI-FULL:v19p109/r5.anchor: أنه من كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام يعني وما يخفي على الذي هو عالم الغيب من شيء في كل مكان

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r4.claim: Nothing is hidden from God; He knows Abraham’s inward and outward condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r4.anchor: استأثرت بعلم الغيب فلا يعزب عن علمك معلوم ، وحالي لا تخفى عليك

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r5.claim: Knowing that God knows all brings rest from worldly intrusions, the translation of anxious thoughts, and distraction over events.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r5.anchor: ومن عرف هذه الجملة استراح من طوارق الأغيار ، واستروح قلبه عن ترجم الأفكار

STUDYQURAN:14:38/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:38/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:38/r1.claim: God knows better than people what will benefit them and is more merciful to them than they are to themselves.
STUDYQURAN:14:38/r1.anchor: God knows more about what will benefit human beings than they do themselves

STUDYQURAN:14:38/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:38/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:38/r2.claim: People must still beseech God to show their servanthood and need for His Mercy, and because supplication hastens the Divine Response.
STUDYQURAN:14:38/r2.anchor: human beings must still beseech God, so that they may manifest their state of servanthood to Him and their need for His Mercy

TAB-FULL:v13p693/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts Abraham leaving Hajar and Ismail in Mecca, after which Abraham says God knows what they conceal and disclose, meaning their grief.
TAB-FULL:v13p693/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: " جاء نبي الله إبراهيم بإسماعيل وهاجر، فوضعهما بمكة في موضع زمزم،

TAB-FULL:v13p701#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p701#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p701#2/r1.claim: Abraham invokes God's knowledge to attest that he seeks God's approval by wanting his child among the obedient, sincere worshippers; God knows their hidden and public states, since all creation is manifest to its Creator and governor.
TAB-FULL:v13p701#2/r1.anchor: فقال: ربنا إنك تعلم ما تخفي قلوبنا عند مسألتنا ما نسألك، وفي غير ذلك من أحوالنا، وما نعلن من دعائنا، فنجهر به

SULAMI:v1p348#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r1.speaker: الخواص
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r1.claim: Al-Khawwas reads what Abraham hides as love of God and what he declares as remembrance of Him.
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r1.anchor: قال الخواص : ما نخفي من حبك وما نعلن

SULAMI:v1p348#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata reads the hidden as spiritual states and the manifest as proper devotional conduct.
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ما نخفي من الأحوال

SULAMI:v1p348#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r3.claim: Abu Uthman urges purifying the secret, cultivating the inner self, and correcting hidden affairs, since nothing is hidden from God.
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : طهر سرك وأعمر باطنك وأصلح خفيات

SULAMI:v1p348#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r4.claim: God alone originates what is absent and brings hidden realities of accord and opposition into view.
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : تفرد الحق بإيجاد المفقودات

SULAMI:v1p348#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r5.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r5.claim: Al-Husayn reads what is hidden as companionship with God and what is declared as ecstatic love.
SULAMI:v1p348#2/r5.anchor: قال الحسين : ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي من الصحبة

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r9.claim: The meaning of Abraham’s statement that God knows what they conceal and disclose is plain.

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r10.claim: The clause about nothing being hidden may continue Abraham’s speech or be God’s own comment; on the first reading, addressing God by name explains why He knows what is hidden and disclosed.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r10.anchor: من تمام كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام أو من كلامه تعالى

TABATABAI:14:37-39/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r11.claim: He suggests “heaven” may mean what is hidden from human perception, while “earth” means what is perceptible to us.
TABATABAI:14:37-39/r11.anchor: المراد بالسماء ما هو خفي علينا غائب عن حسنا

TABRISI:14:37-39/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37-39/r12.claim: Ibrahim acknowledges that God knows what creatures conceal and reveal; nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from Him.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r12.anchor: هذا اعتراف من إبراهيم ع لله سبحانه بأنه يعلم ما يبطن الخلق وما يظهرونه

TABRISI:14:37-39/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37-39/r13.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:14:37-39/r13.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes the statement about nothing hidden from God as a divine aside, not Ibrahim's speech; the quotation resumes with praise in the next verse.
TABRISI:14:37-39/r13.anchor: إنما هو إخبار منه سبحانه بذلك وابتداء كلام من جهته لا على سبيل الحكاية عن إبراهيم ع بل هو اعتراض عن الجبائي

THALABI:v5p322/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p322/r7.claim: God knows all their affairs, whether concealed or made public.
THALABI:v5p322/r7.anchor: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن من جميع أمورنا

THALABI:v5p322/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
THALABI:v5p322/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil include Abraham's affection for Ishmael and his mother, settled in the barren valley, among what is hidden and revealed.
THALABI:v5p322/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومقاتل من الوجد إسماعيل وأمه حيث أسكنها بواد غير ذي زرع

THALABI:v5p322/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r9.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v5p322/r9.claim: Some take the statement that nothing is hidden from God as a parenthetical insertion before the following praise for Abraham's sons.
THALABI:v5p322/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم: هذه صلة فولد إبراهيم (عليه السلام)

THALABI:v5p322/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r10.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v5p322/r10.claim: Others understand God as saying nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from Him, leading into praise for granting Abraham Ishmael and Isaac in old age.
THALABI:v5p322/r10.anchor: وقال الآخرون: قال الله عز وجل وما يخفى على الله وهو قول الله عز وجل الحمد لله الذي وهب لي

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.claim: The account presents Abraham's grateful devotion and supplication as an example of servitude to God, and points to salvation through his monotheistic way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.anchor: Ayrıca Allah’ın verdiği sayısız ve sınırsız nimetlerin şükrünü yerine getiren bir kulun yani Hz. İbrâhim’in Allah’a karşı tutumu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.claim: Commentators say Abraham made the prayer in these verses after Mecca had become a settlement and he and Ishmael had built the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.anchor: Müfessirlere göre İbrâhim bu âyetlerde bildirilen duasını da Mekke yerleşim merkezi haline geldikten ve İsmâil ile birlikte Kâbe’yi inşa ettikten sonra yapmıştır

KHATTABI:v1p56/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p56/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
KHATTABI:v1p56/r1.claim: Abu Bakr is reported to have said on hearing the speech that it could not have come from a human mind.
KHATTABI:v1p56/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه حين طرقت سمعه: أشهد أن هذا الكلام لم يخرج من بال

KHATTABI:v1p56/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p56/r2.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
KHATTABI:v1p56/r2.claim: Amr ibn al-As reports meeting Musaylima, who claimed Muhammad had been sent for grave affairs while his own mission concerned trifles; Musaylima then recited absurd rhymes and issued a rhymed judgment in a palm-tree dispute.
KHATTABI:v1p56/r2.anchor: قال عمرو: فأقبلت حتى مررت على مسيلمة فأعطاني الأمان ثم قال: إن محمدا أرسل في جسيم الأمور وأرسلت في المحقرات

KHATTABI:v1p56/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p56/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p56/r3.claim: The author endorses Amr's judgment that Musaylima was a liar and says his speech has no eloquence, meaning, or wisdom that could rival the Qur'an.
KHATTABI:v1p56/r3.anchor: قلت: صدق عمرو. هل يخالج أحدا شك في ضلالة من هذا سبيله , وسقوط من هذا برهانه ودليله

KHATTABI:v1p56/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p56/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p56/r4.claim: The author calls Musaylima's output base and says later comic writers' nonsense may be more coherent or easier on the ear.
KHATTABI:v1p56/r4.anchor: من السخافات أشف منه وأخف على السمع

KHATTABI:v1p56/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p56/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p56/r5.claim: The author adds an anecdote in which al-Asmaʿi says a man recited bad poetry to Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, who called it like a certain poet's verse.
KHATTABI:v1p56/r5.anchor: حدثنا الأصمعي قال: أنشد رجل أبا عمرو بن العلاء شعرا رديئا

NASHR:v1p232/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p232/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p232/r4.claim: Other meaning-protecting complete stops prevent attributing God's reply to opponents, falsely joining a new clause as a conjunction or adjective, or attaching the next ma to the preceding list; the text gives several examples.
NASHR:v1p232/r4.anchor: فمن التام الوقف على قوله ولا يحزنك قولهم والابتداء إن العزة لله جميعا لئلا يوهم أن ذلك من قولهم
